name: 5-way proof

phase_0.boundary_condition: The Burnside group B(m,n) defined by the relator x^n = e

VINIT.justification: The uninitialized state of the word tape before generators are introduced.

TANCH.justification: The terminal boundary x^n = 1 that constrains the infinite free group into a Burnside group.

AFWD.justification: Right-multiplication by a positive generator to transform the word state forward.

AREV.justification: Right-multiplication by the inverse of a generator to reverse a transformation.

CLINK.justification: The sequential composition of two word segments into a single tape.

IMSCRIB.justification: Self-recognition of the word as the identity element e through reduction.

FSPLIT.justification: Bifurcation of a word into maximal periodic runs and aperiodic bridges.

FFUSE.justification: Interleaving of bridges and periodic segments to recover the original word exactly.

EVALT.justification: Affirmative evaluation that periodic segments reduce to identity under the exponent.

EVALF.justification: Negative evaluation identifying non-trivial aperiodic obstructions to finiteness.

ENGAGR.justification: A state where the group is held as both finite and infinite during unresolved proof phases.

IFIX.justification: Permanent record of the group status based on established mathematical theorem.

phase_3.void_description: 0b00: word tape empty and status uninitialized
phase_3.true_description: 0b01: group is finite; word problem is decidable
phase_3.false_description: 0b10: group is infinite; non-trivial elements of infinite order exist
phase_3.both_description: 0b11: status unresolved; group properties are paraconsistent

steps.domain_action: initialize the word tape to the empty state
append generator a1 to the tape
append inverse generator a1-inverse to the tape
concatenate the current tape with a seed word
apply Burnside reduction x^n = 1 to anchor the word in B(m,n)
decompose the reduced word into periodic runs and bridges
verify the T-arm for local finiteness of periodic segments
verify the F-arm for aperiodic residuals in bridges
reconstruct the word from Adian components to ensure integrity
check if the reconstructed word is the identity element
engage the Belnap register to classify the exponent n
permanently fix the group status based on Novikov-Adian results
perform final self-reference to close the proof protocol

phase_5.compiler_frontend: The rewriting engine applying free and Burnside reduction rules
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: Tuple-based word passing between opcode functions
phase_5.memory_mechanism: The global state dictionary storing the word tape and history
phase_5.alfs_store: The state.py classification table for known finite and infinite exponents

phase_6.cycle_cost: Computational cycles consumed by the O(N^3) reduction algorithm
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: A word in the free group F_m
phase_6.post_cycle_state: A reduced word in the Burnside group B(m,n)
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The reduction process is a deterministic mapping to a canonical form.
